title: Evidence Hound scope file
description: One file of a compliance repo's scope: setup.yaml (organisation, frameworks, domains), controls.yaml (applied controls), audits/<audit>.yaml (one compliance assessment), access.yaml (users, teams and role assignments), settings.yaml (feature flags and general settings), third-parties/<entity>.yaml (one supplier or other third party), capabilities.yaml (which system provides each mitigation), evidence-plan.yaml (how each control's evidence arrives, from whom and how often), ssp.yaml (one system security plan per programme), risks/<study>.yaml (one risk study and its scenarios), or metrics.yaml (metric definitions, instances and dashboards). Guide: docs/scope.md.

metrics.description: metrics.yaml (s16-02): metric definitions, metric instances and dashboards. Samples are not declared: runs write them (source: hound) or people enter them in CISO Assistant. Guide: docs/metrics.md.

metricDefinition.description: What is measured: quantitative with a unit, or qualitative with levels written worst first. A formula computes it from other definitions' instances in the same domain.

domain.description: The domain the definition belongs to; the root folder when left out.

unit.description: count, users, bytes, percentage, score, days, hours or events per second, or a unit added to CISO Assistant's terminologies.

levels.description: For a qualitative metric: two or more levels, worst first.

target.description: A number (from 0 to 100 for a percentage), or for a metric with levels, one of its levels.

expression.description: A CEL expression over the input keys, previous, now and today.

definition.description: A definition's ref_id, or a library definition's URN.

combine.description: How the input's instances in the domain combine; one (the default) reads a single instance.

metricInstance.description: One definition measured in one domain: how often, its target, its owners and the applied controls it tells about.

definition.description: A definition's ref_id, or a library definition's URN.

domain.description: The domain measured; the root folder (all domains) when left out.

target.description: A number (from 0 to 100 for a percentage), or for a metric with levels, one of its levels.

source.description: hound: each run measures it and writes one value for the current period. Left out, people or a formula fill it in.

measure.description: What a run measures, as a percentage: the share of 'checks' passing, of an 'audit''s requirements compliant, of evidence collected in the last week, or of collectors that succeeded.

checks.description: Check ids, or every check below one such as identity.mfa.*.

audit.description: The audit whose requirements requirements_compliant_pct counts, by ref_id.

widget.description: One widget, found again by its title: a metric instance, a builtin metric of one audit, risk study or domain, or text.

builtin.description: The builtin metric, such as progress for an audit or total_scenarios for a risk study.

irp.description: scope/irp.yaml: the incident response plan's programme, version, role holders and judgement sections (s15-09).

version.description: The plan's version; the annual test records it.

roles.description: Who holds each role: an email or a team.

sections.description: The Markdown file of each judgement section, relative to the repo.

reporting.description: reporting.yaml (s15-07): the reports an incident owes, to whom, and within how long of its discovery. Incidents live in CISO Assistant; 'hound incident obligations' lists what one owes.

id.description: Short and stable: a timeline entry 'Reported: <id>, ...' marks the report as made.

report_to.description: Who receives it, and through which channel.

within.description: How long after the incident's discovery the report is due.

when.description: What triggers it: the data kinds an affected system handles, or every incident.

reference.description: The clause that sets the obligation, such as DFARS 252.204-7012(c).

recoveryChecks.description: Checks that set this recovery flag on each run: true only when every one passes (s15-05). The flag itself cannot also be set.

duration.description: A whole number and a unit: m (minutes), h (hours), d (days) or w (weeks).

bia.description: bia/<bia>.yaml (s15-04): one business impact analysis, rated on one risk matrix's impact scale, with one assessment per system.

impact.description: An impact level name from the matrix.

exceptions.description: exceptions.yaml (s15-03): security exceptions requested through the repo. Their status is never declared: an approver sets it in CISO Assistant.

riskStudy.description: risks/<study>.yaml (s15-02): one risk study, rated on one risk matrix by URN, and its scenarios. Risk levels are never declared: CISO Assistant computes them.

matrix.description: The risk matrix's URN, from a library listed in setup.yaml with a snapshot.

systems.description: Impacted systems, by name from setup.yaml.

threats.description: Threats by URN or ref_id, from a library snapshot.

existing_controls.description: Controls in place, by ref_id from controls.yaml.

planned_controls.description: Controls planned to treat the risk, by ref_id from controls.yaml.

riskRating.description: A probability and impact by the matrix's level names; -- is not rated.

requirement.description: A requirement by ref_id, or by URN (a value starting with urn:).

root_folder.description: The existing folder the domains sit under. Default Global.

audit_series.description: The series each system's audit joins when no organisation-wide audit carries it: EX-E8 gives EX-E8-<SYSTEM>, in these periods. Written by hound init.

entity.description: The organisation's own entity (CISO Assistant's main entity). It is only ever updated, never created or deleted.

identifiers.description: Legal identifiers, such as ABN, as name: value.

libraries.description: Other libraries to load: a URN CISO Assistant already stores (such as a mapping set or a built-in risk matrix), or your own library file with its URN, such as a custom risk matrix or threat catalogue (s15-01).

urn.description: The library's URN, as in the file.

file.description: The library file, relative to setup.yaml. Raise its version whenever it changes.

snapshot.description: The snapshot made by 'hound library snapshot', relative to setup.yaml.

programmes.description: The compliance programmes reported on (s11-01): each a framework, the groups reported against and the audit of record. Programmes create nothing in CISO Assistant.

id.description: A lowercase slug, unique, such as essential-eight.

framework.description: A framework URN declared under frameworks, with a snapshot.

groups.description: The implementation groups reported against; each must exist in the framework's snapshot.

audit.description: The ref_id of the audit, or audit series, of record. It uses the programme's framework and belongs to no other programme.

group_by.description: How requirements are grouped in reports: parent (the default) groups them under their parent node.

register.description: The register the programme's reports summarise (s11-14): ai_systems (by screening, use, oversight) or systems (by type).

library.description: The library URN to load from CISO Assistant's stored libraries.

file.description: A custom library file to upload, relative to setup.yaml.

snapshot.description: The framework snapshot (hound framework snapshot), relative to setup.yaml, for offline checks.

tags.description: Per-framework labels, such as an Essentials domain, cui: "true" or a cmmc_asset_category.

cmmc_asset_category.description: The system's CMMC asset category (32 CFR 170.19(c)(1), Table 1), shown in the nist-800-171 system security plan.

solution.description: The ref_id of the supplier's solution this system is. Its supplier must be approved in CISO Assistant before the system is registered.

supplied_through.description: The ref_id of the reseller or provider the contract is with, when not the solution's own supplier; it must be approved too.

objectives.description: Security objectives (s15-04) on CISO Assistant's 0 to 4 scale, such as confidentiality: 3.

recovery.description: Recovery objectives (s15-04) as durations such as 4h or 2d.

ai.description: The system's entry in the AI register (s11-12), with the National AI Centre register template's columns (s11-11): written to CISO Assistant as filtering labels and in the description. See docs/scope.md.

screening.description: The outcome of the National AI Centre's AI screening questions: normal when every answer is no, elevated when any is yes, unacceptable when it is not to be used.

screening_yes.description: The screening questions (1 to 7) answered yes; [] when every answer was no.

screened_on.description: When the screening questions were answered.

registered_on.description: When the system was first added to the register.

version.description: The system's version, where it is needed.

use.description: Built in-house, customised, or a supplier's product (needs 'solution').

purpose.description: Why the system exists and what it aims to achieve.

intended_uses.description: The specific ways it is meant to be used.

limitations.description: What it cannot or should not do: known limitations and prohibited use.

misuse.description: Foreseeable ways it might be misused, or 'None identified.'

data_sources.description: What data it learns from or processes, with its type (text, structured, image, audio).

stakeholders.description: Who might be affected by it.

oversight_note.description: Who can override or switch it off, and the fallback.

impact_assessed_on.description: When the impact assessment was approved.

in_use_from.description: Go-live date; leave out while it is being considered.

last_tested_on.description: The last test or evaluation, on evidence.

domain.description: A domain from setup.yaml; left out for the global domain.

responsible_entity.description: Who implements the control, for the SSP annex (ASD SSP annex template). Without it, hound infers shared when the control covers a system a supplier's solution provides, and consumer otherwise.

documents.description: Ids of documents declared in audit files.

cycle.description: Run the audit in periods: each period is its own audit, its label after the ref_id's organisation and framework, such as EX-E8-Q2-2027FY-BACKUP for EX-E8-BACKUP.

starts.description: The first period's first day: the first of a month, and for a quarter the first day of a financial-year quarter (1 July, 1 October, 1 January or 1 April).

close.description: How an ended period closes: sign_off (the default) locks it once sign_offs records it; auto locks it when it ends.

sign_offs.description: Each ended period's sign-off, so the approval is a reviewed commit.

period.description: The period's label, such as Q2-2027FY or M07-2027FY.

no_evidence.description: What a row with no evidence goes to CISO Assistant as. Default non_compliant: CISO Assistant leaves not-assessed rows out of its compliance percentage, so they would read as compliant. not_assessed opts out.

unlisted.description: What happens to in-group requirements this file does not list.

files.description: Paths or globs, relative to the compliance repo.

provided_by.description: The systems that meet this requirement for the audit, when another system does. The row stays open (never not_applicable) until that system's audit shows the requirement met; hound scope plan lists it under Open dependencies.

access.description: Who can do what in CISO Assistant. Never passwords or tokens: people set their own password from CISO Assistant's invitation.

custom_roles.description: Roles created in CISO Assistant, by name, that 'roles' may name beside the built-in ones.

email.description: The key: the address the person signs in with. Compared without case.

active.description: false keeps the user but blocks sign-in. A user removed from the file is deactivated by 'scope apply --prune', never deleted.

service_account.description: A non-person account: 'publish' (or true) for the collector runner, which needs only analyst; 'apply' for an account that applies the scope.

domain.description: A domain from setup.yaml, or the root folder (Global); left out for the root folder.

email.description: CISO Assistant's team email, which receives the team's task reminders. A team with an email and no leader or members is an owner contact: it is reminded and has no login, so it holds no role.

role_grant.description: A role on a domain, for users and for every member and the leader of teams: one role assignment per user.

role.description: administrator, domain_manager, analyst, approver, auditor, baseline_reader, or a name from custom_roles.

domain.description: A domain from setup.yaml, or the root folder (Global) for the whole organisation.

settings.description: CISO Assistant's feature flags and general settings, by name, as in the settings snapshot of the pinned release (src/EvidenceHound.Core/Scope/ciso-assistant-settings.json). Only the settings named here change. Never secrets such as openai_api_key.

general.description: Each general setting's value, as CISO Assistant stores it.

thirdParty.description: scope/third-parties/<entity>.yaml: one supplier or other third party (a CISO Assistant entity) with its solutions, contracts and representatives.

parent.description: The ref_id of another third party this one belongs to.

domain.description: A domain from setup.yaml; left out for the root folder.

dependency.description: How much the organisation depends on it (0-4).

penetration.description: How far it reaches into the organisation's systems (0-4).

identifiers.description: Legal identifiers by kind, such as LEI or ABN.

solutions.description: ref_ids of this third party's solutions the contract covers.

approved_by.description: Who approved the supplier by making this contract active with hound approve.

approved_on.description: The day it was approved, as yyyy-MM-dd.

customer.description: true when this is a contract a customer (such as a prime) holds with the organisation, rather than one with a supplier.

obligations.description: The clauses the contract imposes. On a customer contract, flow_down marks a clause every supplier handling its data must carry.

clause.description: The clause as the contract names it, such as DFARS 252.204-7012.

framework.description: The URN of the framework the clause requires, declared in setup.yaml.

level.description: The level of that framework the clause requires, such as 2.

data.description: The data kinds the clause covers; none means every supplier.

flow_down.description: On a customer contract only: suppliers handling the data must carry this clause.

forced_tier.description: Hold the supplier at this tier whatever its assessment says; scope plan reports when CISO Assistant's tier differs.

tier.description: A key of the tier scale, such as critical, important, standard or low-impact.

solutions.description: ref_ids of this third party's solutions the assessment covers.

domain.description: The perimeter's domain; the third party's own domain when left out.

questionnaire.description: URN of the questionnaire framework; CISO Assistant creates its audit with the assessment. Declare the framework in scope/setup.yaml.

review_every.description: Open the next review once one falls due, such as 12 months.

conclusions.description: Reviews a person concluded with hound approve; hound scope apply writes each conclusion to CISO Assistant.

review.description: The review: <ref_id>-yyyy-MM by the month it is due, or the assessment's ref_id without a cycle.

on.description: The day it was concluded, as yyyy-MM-dd.

assessments.description: Assessments of this third party. Answers and the tier are CISO Assistant's; hound writes a review's conclusion only when one is recorded under conclusions.

capabilities.description: scope/capabilities.yaml: for one framework, which system in scope provides each mitigation, decided before systems are onboarded. Results stay in each system's own audit.

framework.description: The framework URN, one of setup.yaml's frameworks.

mitigation.description: The mitigation's code: the last part of its parent node's URN, such as ac for application control.

provided_by.description: system (named under systems), manual evidence, or gap (nothing provides it yet).

systems.description: Systems of setup.yaml that provide it.

supplier.description: The third party that supplies it, by ref_id.

route.description: The collector or profile the evidence comes through.

approved_by.description: The role that approved the decision. Required by validation.

signals.description: Signals that pre-filled the answer, each naming its source. A record, never the decision.

evidencePlan.description: scope/evidence-plan.yaml: one row per control (or some of its requirements), saying how its evidence arrives, who provides it and how often. Manual and hybrid rows become recurring CISO Assistant tasks that remind the owner with the runbook.

grc_team.description: The GRC team (a team in access.yaml) that receives and reviews evidence, for rows that do not name their own.

control.description: An applied control's ref_id from controls.yaml.

requirements.description: The requirements (ref or URN) the evidence supports; all the control's when left out.

collector.description: A collector instance's name from hound.yaml, for automated and hybrid rows.

owner.description: The team (in access.yaml) that provides the evidence, for manual and hybrid rows.

grc_team.description: This row's GRC team, if not the file's.

first_due.description: When the first reminder is due, such as a little before the anniversary of an assessment; a past date rolls forward by 'every'. Default: one interval from when the plan is applied.

runbook.description: A Markdown file in the compliance repo: what to export, from where, and how to send it to the GRC team.

sensitiveData.description: The sensitive data a system handles.

kind.description: cui, pii, export_controlled (ITAR, EAR, DSGL) or classified (PSPF, US classified).

detail.description: Which, such as CUI//SP-CTI, ITAR, EAR, DSGL or PROTECTED. Needed for export_controlled and classified.

solutionData.description: The sensitive data a solution handles, each with what approves it.

kind.description: cui, pii, export_controlled (ITAR, EAR, DSGL) or classified (PSPF, US classified).

detail.description: Which, such as CUI//SP-CTI, ITAR, EAR, DSGL or PROTECTED. Needed for export_controlled and classified.

authority.description: What approves the solution for this data, such as FedRAMP Moderate, an IRAP assessment, an ISO 27001 certificate, an export licence or DISP membership.

evidence.description: A document in the repo that shows it.

ssps.description: ssp.yaml: one system security plan per programme (s11-02).

profile.description: The controls annex: ism (ISM controls grouped by Essential Eight strategy) or nist-800-171. The layout is always NIST SP 800-18 Rev 1.

perimeter.description: The plan's boundary: a perimeter declared in setup.yaml.

classification.description: SP 800-18 section 2, system categorisation: for the ISM, the highest classification the system processes, such as OFFICIAL or OFFICIAL: Sensitive.

operational_status.description: SP 800-18 section 7: operational, under development or undergoing a major modification.

system_type.description: SP 800-18 section 8: major application or general support system.

system_owner.description: A user's email or a team from access.yaml.

documents.description: Documents by id from an audit's documents: diagrams, policies and procedures.

sign_offs.description: Signed versions (s11-05): the authorising official's approval of a reviewed draft, by pull request.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the reviewed draft, as 'hound ssp build --snapshot-out' prints it.

snapshot.description: SHA-256 of the snapshot file the draft was built from.

sections.description: The parts that cannot be generated, as Markdown files in the repo, by section name: purpose, environment, management and laws_and_policies (SP 800-18 sections 9, 10, 6 and 12).
